item.title: Your AI Tools at Risk: The Pentagon vs. Anthropic Ruling That Changes Everything
item.description:
A federal judge this week called the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic 'troubling' and an attempt to 'cripple' the company. Marcus and James debate whether this is a dangerous precedent for every AI vendor in the defense supply chain — or proof that the market self-corrects when one vendor plays hardball. Plus: what the OpenAI deal hours later tells you about where the real money flows.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Pulse 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Defense Secretary Hegseth formal notification — March 3, 2026 supply chain risk designation against • President Trump Truth Social post — February 27, 2026 executive order halting all federal Anthropic • Anthropic lawsuit filing — March 10, 2026, Section 3252 free speech and due process claims, potentia • Federal Judge Rita Lin hearing — March 24, 2026, San Francisco, 'cripple' and 'punish' characterizat • Pentagon contract termination — up to $200 million contract value, requirement for affiliated compan
Next episode: If Anthropic wins in court, does every AI safety policy become a First Amendment issue?

item.title: Your 401k This Week: Why the Fed's Tariff Silence Is Actually Bullish
item.description:
The Fed hasn't called an emergency. Hasn't cut rates out of cycle. Hasn't even flinched. This week Marcus and James debate whether that silence is the most bullish signal of 2026 — or just the calm before a very bad storm. Yale's Budget Lab puts tariff costs at $800 per household. J.P. Morgan sees the effective tariff rate hitting 18-20% by mid-2026. What does any of this mean for your 401k right now?
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 04:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Yale Budget Lab (Feb 21, 2026) — Current tariff rate 13.7% (highest since 1941), $1.3T revenue over • Yale Budget Lab — Tariff pass-through to consumers at least 30% for Chinese goods April-December 202 • Yale Budget Lab — Household income loss estimated at $800 annually (short-run, if Section 122 expire • J.P. Morgan (Michael Feroli, Chief U.S. Economist) — Tariffs adding 0.2-0.3% to PCE prices; U.S. eff • J.P. Morgan (Nora Szentivanyi, Senior Global Economist) — Tariff deals (e.g., Vietnam) lifting U.S.
Next episode: If tariff rates hit 18-20% by mid-2026, which sectors get crushed first — and which ones quietly win?
